_comment: RLA(영어) 문제은행 1차 확충 (35문항). 문법은 Grammar 코스 유닛, 독해는 GED 지문분석 유형 기준.

stem_i18n.en: Choose the correct past tense: "Yesterday, she ___ to the market."
stem_i18n.ko: 올바른 과거형을 고르세요: "Yesterday, she ___ to the market."

explanation_i18n.en: "Go" has an irregular past tense: "went". "Gone" needs a helping verb (has gone).
explanation_i18n.ko: "go"의 과거형은 불규칙형 "went"입니다. "gone"은 조동사와 함께 써야 합니다(has gone).

stem_i18n.en: Choose the correct verb: "The list of names ___ on the desk."
stem_i18n.ko: 올바른 동사를 고르세요: "The list of names ___ on the desk."

explanation_i18n.en: The subject is "the list" (singular), not "names". Singular subject takes "is".
explanation_i18n.ko: 주어는 복수 "names"가 아니라 단수 "the list"이므로 "is"를 씁니다.

stem_i18n.en: Choose the correct form: "Right now, the children ___ in the yard."
stem_i18n.ko: 올바른 형태를 고르세요: "Right now, the children ___ in the yard."

explanation_i18n.en: "Right now" signals present progressive: are + -ing.
explanation_i18n.ko: "Right now"는 현재진행형 신호입니다: are + -ing.

stem_i18n.en: Choose the correct form: "By the time we arrived, the movie ___."
stem_i18n.ko: 올바른 형태를 고르세요: "By the time we arrived, the movie ___."

explanation_i18n.en: An action completed before another past action uses past perfect: had started.
explanation_i18n.ko: 과거의 한 시점보다 먼저 끝난 일은 과거완료(had + p.p.)로 씁니다.

stem_i18n.en: Choose the correct pronoun: "This secret stays between you and ___."
stem_i18n.ko: 올바른 대명사를 고르세요: "This secret stays between you and ___."

explanation_i18n.en: After a preposition like "between", use the object pronoun "me".
explanation_i18n.ko: 전치사(between) 뒤에는 목적격 대명사 "me"를 씁니다.

stem_i18n.en: Choose the correct word: "The team celebrated ___ victory."
stem_i18n.ko: 올바른 단어를 고르세요: "The team celebrated ___ victory."

explanation_i18n.en: "Its" (no apostrophe) is possessive. "It's" means "it is".
explanation_i18n.ko: 소유격은 아포스트로피 없는 "its"입니다. "it's"는 "it is"의 축약형입니다.

stem_i18n.en: Choose the correct pronoun: "___ should I say is calling?"
stem_i18n.ko: 올바른 대명사를 고르세요: "___ should I say is calling?"

explanation_i18n.en: The pronoun is the subject of "is calling", so use "who".
explanation_i18n.ko: 이 대명사는 "is calling"의 주어이므로 주격 "who"를 씁니다.

stem_i18n.en: Choose the correct comparison: "This road is ___ than that one."
stem_i18n.ko: 올바른 비교 표현을 고르세요: "This road is ___ than that one."

explanation_i18n.en: Short adjectives form the comparative with -er: longer.
explanation_i18n.ko: 짧은 형용사의 비교급은 -er을 붙입니다: longer.

stem_i18n.en: Which sentence is correct?
stem_i18n.ko: 올바른 문장을 고르세요.

text_i18n.en: He is the most tallest in the class.
He is the tallest in the class.
He is the taller in the class.
He is most tall in the class.

explanation_i18n.en: Use either -est or "most", never both: tallest.
explanation_i18n.ko: 최상급은 -est 또는 most 중 하나만 씁니다: tallest.

stem_i18n.en: Choose the correct word: "She did ___ on the test."
stem_i18n.ko: 올바른 단어를 고르세요: "She did ___ on the test."

explanation_i18n.en: "Well" is the adverb that modifies the verb "did". "Good" is an adjective.
explanation_i18n.ko: 동사 "did"를 꾸미는 부사는 "well"입니다. "good"은 형용사입니다.

stem_i18n.en: Choose the correct preposition: "She is interested ___ science."
stem_i18n.ko: 올바른 전치사를 고르세요: "She is interested ___ science."

explanation_i18n.en: The fixed expression is "interested in".
explanation_i18n.ko: "interested in"이 굳어진 표현입니다.

stem_i18n.en: Complete the pair: "Neither the manager ___ the workers knew about the change."
stem_i18n.ko: 짝을 완성하세요: "Neither the manager ___ the workers knew about the change."

explanation_i18n.en: "Neither" always pairs with "nor".
explanation_i18n.ko: "neither"는 항상 "nor"와 짝을 이룹니다.

stem_i18n.en: Which word best combines the ideas? "___ it was raining, the game continued."
stem_i18n.ko: 두 내용을 잇는 가장 알맞은 말은? "___ it was raining, the game continued."

explanation_i18n.en: The two ideas contrast (rain vs. continuing), so use "Although".
explanation_i18n.ko: 비가 오는데도 경기가 계속됐다는 대조 관계이므로 "Although"가 맞습니다.

stem_i18n.en: Which sentence uses commas correctly?
stem_i18n.ko: 쉼표를 올바르게 쓴 문장은?

text_i18n.en: We bought apples bananas, and grapes.
We bought, apples, bananas and grapes.
We bought apples, bananas, and grapes.
We bought apples, bananas and, grapes.

explanation_i18n.en: Separate every item in a list with commas: apples, bananas, and grapes.
explanation_i18n.ko: 나열되는 항목 사이마다 쉼표를 씁니다: apples, bananas, and grapes.

stem_i18n.en: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
stem_i18n.ko: 구두점이 올바른 문장은?

text_i18n.en: After the storm we cleaned the yard.
After the storm, we cleaned the yard.
After, the storm we cleaned the yard.
After the storm we cleaned, the yard.

explanation_i18n.en: Put a comma after an introductory phrase: "After the storm,".
explanation_i18n.ko: 문장 앞에 오는 도입구 뒤에는 쉼표를 씁니다: "After the storm,".

stem_i18n.en: Choose the correct possessive: "The ___ leashes are hanging by the door." (two dogs)
stem_i18n.ko: 올바른 소유격을 고르세요: "The ___ leashes are hanging by the door." (개 두 마리)

explanation_i18n.en: Plural noun ending in s takes only an apostrophe: dogs'.
explanation_i18n.ko: s로 끝나는 복수명사의 소유격은 아포스트로피만 붙입니다: dogs'.

stem_i18n.en: Choose the correct word: "___ going to love this book."
stem_i18n.ko: 올바른 단어를 고르세요: "___ going to love this book."

explanation_i18n.en: "You're" = "you are". "Your" shows possession.
explanation_i18n.ko: "You're"는 "you are"의 축약형입니다. "your"는 소유격입니다.

stem_i18n.en: Which sentence uses a semicolon correctly?
stem_i18n.ko: 세미콜론을 올바르게 쓴 문장은?

text_i18n.en: I finished the test; and left the room.
The rain stopped; the sun came out.
Because it was late; we went home.

explanation_i18n.en: A semicolon joins two complete sentences that are closely related.
explanation_i18n.ko: 세미콜론은 서로 관련된 두 개의 완전한 문장을 연결합니다.

stem_i18n.en: Which sentence uses a colon correctly?
stem_i18n.ko: 콜론을 올바르게 쓴 문장은?

text_i18n.en: You will need: paper, a pen, and a ruler.
Bring the following: paper, a pen, and a ruler.
Bring: the following paper, a pen, and a ruler.
You will: need paper, a pen, and a ruler.

explanation_i18n.en: A colon follows a complete sentence to introduce a list.
explanation_i18n.ko: 콜론은 완전한 문장 뒤에서 목록을 소개할 때 씁니다.

stem_i18n.en: Which of the following is a sentence fragment?
stem_i18n.ko: 다음 중 조각문(완전하지 않은 문장)은?

explanation_i18n.en: "Running down the empty hallway" has no subject or main verb.
explanation_i18n.ko: "Running down the empty hallway"에는 주어와 본동사가 없습니다.

stem_i18n.en: Which is the best way to fix this run-on? "The bus was late we missed the meeting."
stem_i18n.ko: 다음 이어진 문장(run-on)을 고치는 가장 좋은 방법은? "The bus was late we missed the meeting."

text_i18n.en: The bus was late, we missed the meeting.
The bus was late, so we missed the meeting.
The bus was late we, missed the meeting.
The bus, was late we missed the meeting.

explanation_i18n.en: Join two sentences with a comma + conjunction (so). A comma alone creates a comma splice.
explanation_i18n.ko: 두 문장은 쉼표 + 접속사(so)로 연결합니다. 쉼표만 쓰면 쉼표 오용(comma splice)입니다.

stem_i18n.en: Which sentence is a compound sentence?
stem_i18n.ko: 다음 중 중문(두 개의 독립절)은?

text_i18n.en: When the sun set, we left.
I cooked dinner, and she washed the dishes.

explanation_i18n.en: Two independent clauses joined by ", and" make a compound sentence.
explanation_i18n.ko: 두 개의 독립절이 ", and"로 연결되면 중문입니다.

stem_i18n.en: In "Although he was tired, he finished the report," the clause "Although he was tired" is…
stem_i18n.ko: "Although he was tired, he finished the report"에서 "Although he was tired"는 무엇인가요?

explanation_i18n.en: It starts with the subordinating word "although" and cannot stand alone.
explanation_i18n.ko: 종속접속사 "although"로 시작하며 홀로 문장이 될 수 없는 종속절입니다.

stem_i18n.en: Which sentence is capitalized correctly?
stem_i18n.ko: 대문자를 올바르게 쓴 문장은?

text_i18n.en: my cousin lives in chiang mai, thailand.
My cousin lives in Chiang Mai, Thailand.
My Cousin lives in chiang mai, Thailand.
my Cousin lives in Chiang mai, thailand.

explanation_i18n.en: Capitalize the first word and proper nouns (Chiang Mai, Thailand).
explanation_i18n.ko: 문장 첫 단어와 고유명사(Chiang Mai, Thailand)는 대문자로 씁니다.

stem_i18n.en: Choose the correct word: "They left ___ shoes by the door."
stem_i18n.ko: 올바른 단어를 고르세요: "They left ___ shoes by the door."

explanation_i18n.en: "Their" shows possession. "There" is a place; "they're" = "they are".
explanation_i18n.ko: 소유격은 "their"입니다. "there"는 장소, "they're"는 "they are"입니다.

stem_i18n.en: Choose the correct word: "The new schedule will ___ everyone in the office."
stem_i18n.ko: 올바른 단어를 고르세요: "The new schedule will ___ everyone in the office."

explanation_i18n.en: "Affect" is the verb (to influence); "effect" is usually a noun.
explanation_i18n.ko: 동사(영향을 주다)는 "affect", "effect"는 주로 명사(결과)입니다.

stem_i18n.en: Which revision removes the redundancy? "He returned back to his hometown."
stem_i18n.ko: 중복 표현을 없앤 수정은? "He returned back to his hometown."

text_i18n.en: He returned back again to his hometown.
He went returned to his hometown.
He returned backwards to his hometown.

explanation_i18n.en: "Return" already means "go back", so "back" is redundant.
explanation_i18n.ko: "return"에 이미 "돌아가다"라는 뜻이 있어 "back"은 중복입니다.

stem_i18n.en: Which sentence is most appropriate for a formal job application letter?
stem_i18n.ko: 격식 있는 입사 지원서에 가장 알맞은 문장은?

text_i18n.en: Hey, I really wanna work for you guys.
I would welcome the opportunity to join your team.
Gimme a chance, you won't regret it!

explanation_i18n.en: Formal writing avoids slang and casual phrases.
explanation_i18n.ko: 격식체에서는 속어와 구어체 표현을 피합니다.

stem_i18n.en: "Recycling one aluminum can saves enough energy to run a TV for three hours. Yet most cans still end up in landfills. Better recycling habits could save huge amounts of energy every year." — What is the main idea?
stem_i18n.ko: "Recycling one aluminum can..." 지문의 중심 생각은?

text_i18n.en: Recycling cans could save significant energy.

explanation_i18n.en: Every sentence supports the point that recycling cans saves energy.
explanation_i18n.ko: 모든 문장이 '캔 재활용이 에너지를 절약한다'는 핵심을 뒷받침합니다.

stem_i18n.en: "Small daily habits shape long-term success. Reading ten minutes a day adds up to dozens of books over a decade. Saving a little each week grows into real savings. Big goals are usually reached through small, repeated actions." — Which title fits best?
stem_i18n.ko: "Small daily habits..." 지문에 가장 어울리는 제목은?

explanation_i18n.en: Reading and saving are examples; the passage is about small habits leading to big results.
explanation_i18n.ko: 독서와 저축은 예시일 뿐이고, 글 전체는 작은 습관이 큰 결과를 만든다는 내용입니다.

stem_i18n.en: "Dara checked the sky, packed an umbrella, and moved the picnic food back into the fridge." — What can you infer?
stem_i18n.ko: "Dara checked the sky..." 에서 추론할 수 있는 것은?

explanation_i18n.en: Checking the sky, packing an umbrella, and postponing the picnic all suggest expected rain.
explanation_i18n.ko: 하늘을 살피고 우산을 챙기고 소풍 음식을 넣어둔 행동 모두 비를 예상한다는 단서입니다.

stem_i18n.en: "The waiting room was full, and the receptionist kept apologizing for the delay. Several patients sighed and glanced at the clock." — How do the patients most likely feel?
stem_i18n.ko: "The waiting room was full..." 에서 환자들의 기분은?

explanation_i18n.en: Sighing and glancing at the clock are signs of frustration with waiting.
explanation_i18n.ko: 한숨을 쉬고 시계를 자꾸 보는 행동은 기다림에 대한 답답함(frustration)의 표시입니다.

stem_i18n.en: "The library is open 9–6 on weekdays and 10–2 on Saturdays. It is closed on Sundays and public holidays." — When does the library open on Saturday?
stem_i18n.ko: "The library is open..." — 토요일 개관 시간은?

explanation_i18n.en: The passage says Saturdays are 10–2, so it opens at 10 a.m.
explanation_i18n.ko: 토요일은 10–2시로 명시되어 있으므로 오전 10시에 엽니다.

stem_i18n.en: "Don't wait until it's too late — schedule your free dental checkup today and keep your smile healthy for years to come!" — What is the author's main purpose?
stem_i18n.ko: "Don't wait until it's too late..." 글쓴이의 주된 목적은?

text_i18n.en: To entertain readers with a story
To persuade readers to get a checkup

explanation_i18n.en: Commands like "schedule today" and emotional appeals are persuasive techniques.
explanation_i18n.ko: "오늘 예약하세요" 같은 권유와 감정에 호소하는 표현은 설득이 목적임을 보여줍니다.

stem_i18n.en: "The instructions were so ambiguous that half the class did the assignment one way and half did it another." — What does "ambiguous" most nearly mean?
stem_i18n.ko: "The instructions were so ambiguous..." 에서 "ambiguous"의 뜻에 가장 가까운 것은?

explanation_i18n.en: The class understood it two different ways, so the instructions were unclear.
explanation_i18n.ko: 학생들이 두 가지로 다르게 이해했다는 것은 지시가 불명확했다는 뜻입니다.
